learn: Cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition.
Each one affects long-term health.
A balanced program trains all five.
check: Body composition is the ratio of...
lessons.try: Rate yourself 1-5 on each component and explain why.

learn: Agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time and speed.
Power combines strength and speed, as in a vertical jump.
These improve with sport-specific practice.
lessons.try: Test your vertical jump and reaction time.

learn: Use standard tests: PACER, push-ups, curl-ups, sit-and-reach, trunk lift.
Compare to healthy fitness zones for your age.
Re-test regularly to measure progress.
lessons.try: Complete a fitness assessment and record results.

learn: Overload: work harder than normal to improve.
Progression: increase gradually. Specificity: train for your goal.
Reversibility: fitness fades if you stop training.
check: Training for your specific goal is...
lessons.try: Explain each principle with an example.

learn: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type.
For cardio: 3-5 days a week, moderate to vigorous, 20-60 minutes.
For strength: 2-3 non-consecutive days a week.
check: Strength training should be on ___ days.
Cardio is recommended ___ days a week.
The T at the end of FITT is...
lessons.try: Write a four-week FITT plan.

learn: Warm up, cool down and stretch.
Use proper technique and equipment; stay hydrated.
Overtraining causes injury; rest and recovery are part of training.
lessons.try: Make a safety checklist for a workout.

learn: Macronutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats) provide energy.
Micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) support body functions: calcium for bones, iron for blood.
Water is essential for every system.
lessons.try: Track your macronutrients for one day.

learn: Choose whole foods over highly processed ones.
Read labels for added sugar, sodium and saturated fat.
Plan balanced meals and snacks.
lessons.try: Plan a day of balanced meals.

learn: Family, culture, friends, advertising and cost all influence choices.
Advertisements often target teens with sugary products.
Media literacy helps you make your own decisions.
lessons.try: Analyse a food advertisement's techniques.

learn: Teens need 8-10 hours of sleep a night.
Teen body clocks shift later, making early mornings hard.
Good sleep habits: a regular schedule, no screens an hour before bed, a dark cool room.
lessons.try: Track your sleep for a week and set a goal.

learn: Stress triggers the "fight or flight" response.
Chronic stress harms health; healthy coping helps.
Strategies: exercise, breathing, time management, talking, hobbies, sleep.
lessons.try: Make a personal stress toolkit.

learn: Mental health includes emotional, psychological and social wellbeing.
Anxiety and depression are common and treatable.
Reach out to a trusted adult, counsellor or helpline; in the US you can call or text 988.
check: In the US, a mental health helpline is...
lessons.try: Make a list of support resources.

learn: Respect, trust, honesty, support and equality.
Healthy relationships allow independence and other friendships.
Boundaries are limits that protect your wellbeing.
lessons.try: List your personal boundaries.

learn: Control, jealousy, pressure, threats and isolation are warning signs.
Digital abuse includes constant monitoring or pressure to share passwords or images.
Tell a trusted adult if you see warning signs.
check: If you see warning signs, tell...
lessons.try: Identify warning signs in sample scenarios.

learn: Communicate assertively with "I" statements.
Consent means freely agreeing; it can be withdrawn at any time.
Respect "no" in every situation.
lessons.try: Practise assertive responses to pressure.

learn: Nicotine is highly addictive and harms brain development.
Many vapes contain as much nicotine as a pack of cigarettes or more.
Vaping can cause lung injury and addiction.
lessons.try: Create a public service announcement about vaping.

learn: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination and memory.
Misusing prescription medicines is dangerous and illegal.
Teen brains are especially vulnerable to addiction.
check: Teen brains are ___ vulnerable to addiction.
lessons.try: Discuss why the teen brain is more vulnerable.

learn: Most teens don't use substances; knowing this reduces pressure.
Refusal skills: say no, give a reason, suggest an alternative, leave.
Healthy alternatives: sports, arts, clubs, friends.
lessons.try: Write a script for refusing pressure.

learn: Check, call, care: check the scene and person, call 911, give care.
Give your location and stay on the line.
Don't move someone with a possible spinal injury.
check: The steps are check, call and...
On an emergency call, give your...
Don't move someone with a possible...
lessons.try: Role-play an emergency call.

learn: Sprains: RICE (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
Burns: cool running water for 10-20 minutes.
Heat exhaustion: move to shade, cool down, drink water; heat stroke is an emergency.
lessons.try: Make a first-aid card for sports.

learn: CPR keeps blood flowing when the heart stops.
Hands-only CPR: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest.
AEDs give voice instructions; take a certified course to learn.
check: To learn CPR properly, take a...
lessons.try: Find where the AEDs are in your school.

learn: The muscular and skeletal systems move the body.
The cardiovascular and respiratory systems deliver oxygen.
The nervous system coordinates everything.
check: Oxygen is delivered by the cardiovascular and ___ systems.
lessons.try: Explain how three systems work together during running.

learn: Puberty brings growth spurts, hormonal changes and emotional changes.
Everyone develops at their own pace.
Good nutrition and sleep support growth.
lessons.try: Write questions about growth to ask a trusted adult or doctor.

learn: Wash hands, get vaccinated, eat well and exercise.
Chronic diseases like heart disease and type 2 diabetes are linked to lifestyle.
Regular check-ups catch problems early.
lessons.try: Make a personal health plan.

learn: Offence: create space, move without the ball, pass and shoot.
Defence: mark players, close passing lanes, communicate.
Transition is the switch between offence and defence.
check: The switch between offence and defence is...
lessons.try: Play a small-sided game and practise transitions.

learn: Captains lead by example, encourage teammates and stay calm.
Everyone has a role; supporting each other wins games.
Feedback should be specific and positive.
lessons.try: Lead a warm-up for your team.

learn: Follow rules, respect officials and opponents.
Win and lose with grace.
Sportsmanship builds character beyond sport.
check: After a loss, a good sport...
lessons.try: Write a team code of conduct.

learn: Choose activities you enjoy: walking, swimming, cycling, dance, martial arts, hiking.
Activities with friends and family are easier to keep up.
Try new activities to find what you love.
check: Activities are easier to keep up when...
lessons.try: Try a new activity and write about it.

learn: Set short-term (weeks) and long-term (months, years) goals.
Use SMART goals and track progress.
Adjust goals as you grow.
lessons.try: Write a one-year fitness goal and monthly steps.

learn: Parks, community centres and clubs offer activities.
Volunteering at sports events builds skills.
Active communities are healthier communities.
lessons.try: Find three free places to be active near you.
